_meta.templatePurpose: Structured sidecar for one implementation-plan.md document describing one intended body of work performed under a workflow and, when applicable, governed through a Klinswork Work Unit.
_meta.authorityRule: The implementation-plan.md is the authoritative human-readable plan. This sidecar is a structured description of that plan and must not replace the Work Unit Registry, Work Unit Activities, Work Implementation Session, workflow specification, documentation-run state, execution evidence, final summary, or work-update sidecar.
_meta.designShiftIn31: Version 3.1 added semantic context resolution through stable Resource IDs, Startup provenance, Project/System/Application/Resource placement, authoritative-resource declarations, and explicit support for plans created after some work had already begun.
_meta.designShiftIn32: Version 3.2 adds first-class Work Unit linkage, Work Unit state-at-plan-creation, activation-gate representation, formal Work Implementation Session linkage, and allocated Work Unit Activity references without moving current-state or execution-history authority into the plan sidecar.
_meta.resourceResolutionPrinciple: A workflow should declare the context it needs; the Resource Registry resolves those requirements to stable Resource IDs and current locations.
_meta.indirectionPrinciple: Implementation plans should depend on stable resource identities and authority roles rather than hard-coded physical URLs whenever registered resources exist.
_meta.planningTruthRule: Do not represent work completed before plan creation as though it had been prospectively planned.
_meta.workUnitAuthorityRule: The Work Unit Registry is authoritative for current Work Unit state. This sidecar may snapshot Work Unit state at plan creation and describe the plan's relationship to the Work Unit, but it must not become a competing Work Unit record.
_meta.sessionAuthorityRule: A Work Implementation Session is the authoritative human-readable execution record for one bounded formal session. This sidecar may link to session records and describe activation relationships, but it must not absorb session execution history.
_meta.wuaAuthorityRule: Work Unit Activities are the append-oriented timestamped history of material Work Unit events. Reference only WUA IDs already allocated by the Work Unit Activities authority; never pre-allocate future WUA IDs in an implementation-plan sidecar.
_meta.jsonCommentConvention: JSON does not support native comments. Keys named _meta, _comment, or _fieldNotes are intentional schema commentary and should be ignored by consumers that only need operational values.

risks.mitigation: Maintain explicit Project → System distinction in every relevant record.

risks.risk: Roadmap intent becomes current truth: Planned Work Queue capabilities are described as implemented.

risks.risk: Invented identity: A PROJ-###, SYS-###, relationship ID, run ID, or session ID is created merely to fill a blank.

risks.risk: Repository path becomes semantic authority: Physical location is treated as proof of Project/System ownership or identity.
risks.mitigation: Keep path/locality rules separate from identity and relationship authority.

risks.risk: Building Map ownership drift: Task Assignment and Tracking is incorrectly made owner of Building Map governance.
risks.mitigation: Preserve Building Map / Locations as a shared dependency and relationship.

risks.risk: Excessive WUA granularity: Every edit becomes a Work Unit Activity, making history noisy and unusable.
Insufficient WUA history: Important session/state transitions happen without timestamped Work Unit history.
Reconstructed plan falsifies chronology: Already-completed work is presented as prospectively planned.
System Summary becomes implementation archaeology: Documentation expands indefinitely into exhaustive reconstruction of every historical Work Queue version.
risks.mitigation: Document enough to establish current System meaning, history, uncertainty, and next verification; defer exhaustive chronology.

general.summary: A bounded documentation implementation plan for completing the second Klinswork Project Definition exemplar.
keyPoints: Task Assignment and Tracking is the Project; Work Queue is the principal System.
The plan is reconstructed-continuation because some Project records existed before plan creation.
The plan governs remaining work from 2026-08-16T07:53:00-06:00 forward.

technical.summary: The plan creates a Project/System documentation package, companion sidecars, Viewer/discovery validation, and Registry/session reconciliation.
keyPoints: Project Summary and System Summary are separate authorities.
Roadmap intent remains separate from current-state evidence.
Work Unit current state, WUA history, implementation plan, and formal session execution have distinct authority roles.
No unsupported durable IDs may be invented.

technical._comment: Technical inventories describe the plan/document. Do not use URLs here as substitutes for stable Resource IDs when a registered resource exists.

publication._comment: Publication fields describe the implementation-plan document/sidecar publication state, not deployment of the implementation target.

deployment._comment: Deployment describes planned or relevant target deployments. Stable resource identity should remain separate from deployment URL.

validation._comment: Profile-level semantic validation rules for implementation-plan sidecars.
rules: The implementation-plan.md is authoritative; this sidecar describes it.
The Work Unit Registry is authoritative for current Work Unit state; workUnitContext.stateAtPlanCreation is a plan-time snapshot only.
Work Unit Activities are authoritative for timestamped material Work Unit history; this sidecar may reference allocated WUA IDs but must not pre-allocate future WUA IDs.
A Work Implementation Session is authoritative for detailed formal-session execution history; this sidecar may link to session records but must not absorb execution evidence.
Session initiation and session activation must remain distinguishable when an activation gate exists.
Registered resources should be referenced by stable Resource ID when known.
Unknown Work Unit Activity, Session, Project, System, Application, Relationship, or Resource identifiers must remain blank rather than be invented.
A WORK-#### identifier must be used only when allocated by the Work Unit authority.
Project/System/Application/Resource placement must not be inferred from repository path alone.
Startup context and session-specific working context must remain distinct.
The workflow declares required context; the Resource Registry resolves that context.
A reconstructed-continuation plan must identify its planning boundary and prior-work basis.
Work completed before plan creation must not be represented as prospectively planned work.
currentState must describe the state at the plan boundary.
plannedTests must remain distinct from tests actually executed.
Resource identity must remain distinct from current physical location or deployment URL.

The implementation-plan sidecar must not become a substitute for Work Unit current state, Work Unit Activity history, formal-session execution history, workflow-run history, final evidence, summary, or work-update records.
notes: WORK-0001 and WUA-0003 are taken directly from the source implementation plan.
No future WUA ID was pre-allocated.
Permanent Project, System, Session, Relationship, Run, and unsupported Resource IDs remain blank.
Work Unit state is represented as a plan-time snapshot rather than current-state authority.
Actual planned-test execution remains outside this sidecar.

interpretationNotes: The source implementation plan is treated as the authority for populated plan facts.
The uploaded filename is used as document.filePath because no verified repository location for this uploaded copy was supplied.
The plan's intended repository target for the governing plan is described in its implementation stages but is not asserted here as the current physical location.
Stable Resource IDs not supplied by the source plan are left blank rather than inferred from outside the source.
unresolvedQuestions: What stable Resource ID identifies the Work Unit Registry workbook in this record context?
What permanent Project ID will eventually be allocated to Task Assignment and Tracking?
What permanent System ID will eventually be allocated to Work Queue, if the System identity architecture adopts one?
What canonical repository filename/path should be used when this uploaded plan is installed in the Project repository?
provenance._comment: Preserve the evidence used to construct the sidecar. For reconstructed-continuation plans, explicitly record reconstruction sources and interpretation limits. Work Unit/session/WUA references must be grounded in their respective authorities.
contextResolutionNotes: The plan identifies the required authority roles and sources; stable Resource IDs are populated only when directly supported by the source.
reconstructionNotes: Project Identity, Project README, and Project Summary predate the plan boundary.
